key_insight: PatternMiner combines LLM reasoning with small-model training and interpretability to turn patterns in mathematical data into iteratively refined conjectures and proofs.
engineering_relevance: The system illustrates how an LLM agent can coordinate data generation, model training, interpretation, and mathematical software in an automated discovery workflow.
method: Generate mathematical datasets from a broad question and train small models.
Interpret learned patterns to formulate conjectures.
Search for counterexamples, refine conjectures or retrain, and attempt proofs.
evidence_signal: Across five well-known positivity problems in algebraic combinatorics, the authors report several new theorems, including a restricted Kazhdan–Lusztig combinatorial invariance result.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify success rates or computational costs, leaving reliability and scalability beyond these case studies unclear.
paper_title: PatternMiner: Automated Mathematical Discovery Through LLM-Guided Training and Interpretation of Small Models
